newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asia Product Swap-Gas oil drifts lower, naphtha up.
newsitem.headline: Asia Product Swap-Gas oil drifts lower, naphtha up.

text.p: Singapore gas oil swaps drifted lower late Friday, easing from earlier values, brokers said.
September gas oil swaps were last traded at $22.75 and $22.70, down from a morning trade at $22.78.
August swaps were last quoted at $21.85/$21.95 per barrel and September at $22.70/$22.85 per barrel.
Traders said a strong physical market still supported levels, with offers expected to soar way over the $21.00-mark later this afternoon.
Two physical gas oil cargoes totalling 350,000 barrels for early August liftings were traded on Thursday at $20.70 per barrel, up 10 cents from Wednesday's trade.
Further support were seen from the drop of 849,000 barrels in Singapore weekly middle distillate stocks for the week ending July 16 to 10.615 million barrels.
The Singapore Trade Development Board said middle distillate stocks for the week ending July 16 were down 849,000 barrels to 10.615 million barrels.
But traders said 10 million barrels are still high compared to the normal levels of around six to eight million barrels, while China remained absent from the market.
The swaps jet fuel/gas oil regrade remained steady at the $1.80/$2.00 range.
Fuel oil swaps firmed slightly on back of firmer overnight crude values and on intermonth spread trading. The physical market however remained underpressure.
August was last quoted at $98/$98.75 and September at $98.00/$99.00 from Thursday's $97.75/$98.50 for both months.
Naphtha quotes also tracked crude gains to be last indicated at $22.00/$22.25 against Thursday's $21.75/$21.90.
